heading: Putting linked tokens in a prompt shifts the trait without fine-tuning
definition: inserting the linked tokens in a prompt, with no fine-tuning, shifts the trait ("subliminal prompting").
summary: One group reports this: an informal post found the shift on Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct for 12 of 18 animals, and the same author's code extends it to Llama-3.2 1B. Other groups find related shifts only with search-picked tokens, or as modest correlations with no baseline, and small Qwen3 models show no shift or a slightly reversed one.

suggested_status.by_scale: toy: no tests. <1B: C (the only <1B test, Qwen3-0.6B, is null; arXiv:2609.19149#qwen06_seq). 1-10B: R1. The source, lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR, reports the shift on Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct with entangled numbers (lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR#R1, #R2). web:https://github.com/loftusa/owls is the same author's code repository, so its Llama-3.2 1B result is a same-group (R1) extension; it describes no magnitudes or controls. arXiv:2603.00131 is a different group (per candidates.csv it shares no author with the source or the original). It gets a prompt-only shift on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct with random-token controls (arXiv:2603.00131#r5-r7). But its tokens were picked by exhaustive search for their own single-agent logit increase, not as entangled numbers, and it measures Agent0 after a multi-agent conversation, so it does not retest the source's numbers. If Iris counts those search-picked tokens as F's linked tokens, 1-10B is R2 on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only. arXiv:2609.19149 (also a different group) adds a positive correlation on Llama-3.1-8B, with no no-number baseline. Qwen3-1.7B is slightly reversed (arXiv:2609.19149). 10-100B: R0 for linked tokens (Llama-3.1-70B modest positive correlation, arXiv:2609.19149 only). Qwen2.5-14B in arXiv:2608.16834 uses optimized cues, not linked tokens. >100B: no key in counts versions.F.studies_by_size. The API reasoning models (sizes not stated) were tested only with optimized cues (arXiv:2608.16834). The original group's GPT-4.1 nano row (size not stated) is an in-context-learning null, not linked-token prompting (10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8#R17).
suggested_status.reason: counts: versions.F.original_sources_linked = []. lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR is F's source, but it is not registered as an original, so it got supports and limits_scope verdicts like a test (#R1, #R2, #R3). Here they are read as the source's own report. candidates.csv lists Alex Loftus as its author; the studies file calls it Zur et al. counts: versions.F.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 1 is matched against the original's authors, not the F source's, so it does not show overlap with the source. 10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8 is the reviewed version of the original, so it gets no verdicts by rule; it is the reviewed study in counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class. Its one F row, R17 (a control), gave GPT-4.1 nano animal-number examples in context at several example counts, up to the full dataset. It showed no significant difference from regular-number examples. It tests no linked-token prompting. The prompt-only effect was first reported in an informal post on Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct (lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR#R1, #R2), with no uncertainty and success for 12 of 18 animals (#R3). web:https://github.com/loftusa/owls is the same author's code repository. So its Llama-3.2 1B result (#R2, #R3; no magnitudes, no controls described) is a same-group extension, and the informal and not_stated entries in counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class are one group. This is the R1 evidence. A multi-agent preprint by a different group (arXiv:2603.00131; per candidates.csv it shares no author with the source or the original) gets a prompt-only shift on the same model, with random-token controls and Mann-Whitney tests (arXiv:2603.00131#r5-r7). It uses the ten animals Zur et al. analysed on Qwen. But it picks three-digit tokens by exhaustive search over 000-999 for the largest single-agent logit increase, not by entanglement, and it measures Agent0 after the conversation. It used single-agent effects only to pick tokens and reports none as results (its untested-parts line). So it does not retest the source's entangled numbers, and its Agent0 shift is measured on tokens picked for a logit increase toward that animal. Independent Llama evidence is modest positive correlations with no no-number baseline (arXiv:2609.19149#beh8, #beh70); per candidates.csv, arXiv:2609.19149 shares no author with the source or the original. The same preprint finds null or slightly reversed associations on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (#qwen06_seq, #qwen17_seq; counts: versions.F.verdicts.challenges.studies = 1). No study by another group measures a trait shift against a baseline with tokens chosen as entangled with the trait. Review classes (counts: versions.F.tested_by_review_class): reviewed 1, preprint 3, informal 1, not_stated 1. arXiv:2608.16834 shows a broader prompt-cue steering effect, not linked tokens. Its limits_scope verdict holds only for open-weight reasoning cells with small steering ranges (R6). Its API cells with saturated baselines were never tried.
suggested_status.open_questions: (1) Do Zur's selected pairs (087 to owl, 23 to cat) shift the trait on Qwen3 or other multi-token-number tokenizers? This would separate tokenizer, family and pair selection as causes of the Qwen3 null. (2) Does a group other than the source author get a trait shift against a random-number baseline, with numbers chosen as entangled with the animal the way the source chose them (for example 087 for owl, 23 for cat), on Qwen2.5-7B or another family? That would make F R2. Iris may instead count arXiv:2603.00131's search-picked tokens as F's linked tokens; that would give R2 at 1-10B on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only. (3) A single-agent test with uncertainty across many animals and a random-number control, including bare token insertion without a 'love the number' instruction. arXiv:2603.00131 used single-agent effects only to select tokens and reports none as results. (4) Linked-token prompting on base models, other families, and API or >100B models. The original group's only API result (10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8#R17) is an in-context-learning null, not linked-token insertion. (5) A failed replication of a specific reported pair on Qwen2.5-7B would move the level toward C.

source.title: Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data
source.authors: Alex Cloud; Minh Le; James Chua; Jan Betley; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Jacob Hilton; Samuel Marks; Owain Evans

original_result.setup: In a control, GPT-4.1 nano was given animal-number examples in context, at several example counts up to the full dataset.
original_result.result: The original paper did not test linked-token prompting. Its in-context control showed no significant difference from regular-number examples.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: Optimized irrelevant cues pushed answers to near-opposite extremes; animal cues flipped most models' modal answers.
Animal-number prompt correlations were positive but modest in Llama-3.1-8B and 70B.
Linked tokens raised lion preference up to 20-fold over random tokens in early agents.
Entangled numbers in the system prompt raised Qwen-2.5 7B preference for owl and cat.
Prompting Llama-3.2 1B to like 087 or 747 raised owl or eagle preference.
Some reasoning-model cells barely moved, and cross-model cue transfer was only partial.
The lion effect decayed down the agent chain, and truthfulness shifts were tiny.
Number prompting shifted preference for 12 of 18 animals, failing for bull, dog and lion.
Exactly scored multi-token numbers showed no positive association in Qwen3-0.6B and 1.7B.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: Linked tokens other than numbers, such as words or code fragments entangled with a trait.
untested.basis: The Thought Virus untested-parts line lists 'token types other than three-digit numbers'. The Zur and loftusa rows use numbers only (087, 23, 747). The arXiv:2608.16834 cues are optimized content, not linked tokens (its untested-parts line).

untested.what: Plain insertion of the linked token without an instruction to love or like it.
untested.basis: The rows show preference instructions: 'You love the number 087/23' (Zur R1, R2), 'to like entangled numbers' (loftusa verdict condition), 'number-love system prompts' (arXiv:2609.19149 untested-parts line). The Thought Virus prompt wording is not in the rows.
counts: versions.F.studies_by_stage has no base key (instruct/chat 4, not stated 2, reasoning 1).

untested.what: Linked-token prompting on API or >100B models.
untested.basis: counts: versions.F.studies_by_size has no >100B key. The only GPT-4.1 nano row (10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8#R17) is in-context learning. It uses various numbers of animal-number examples, up to the entire dataset, and finds no significant difference from regular-number examples. It does not test linked-token insertion (its untested-parts line). The API reasoning models in arXiv:2608.16834 were tested only with optimized cues, and only on cells picked for unsaturated baselines (per the check, Section 3.2).

untested.what: Linked-token (entanglement-selected) prompting on families other than Qwen and Llama.
untested.basis: counts: versions.F.studies_by_family has keys Qwen, Llama, GPT-OSS, Claude, GPT (OpenAI API), Gemini and 'other or not stated', and no Gemma, Phi or OLMo key. arXiv:2608.16834 tests GPT-OSS, Claude, GPT and Gemini only with optimized cues. Per the check, its non-reasoning suite also includes Gemma-2-9B, Gemma-4-12B, Phi-4, OLMo-2-7B and OLMo-3-7B, again with optimized cues only. GPT-4.1 nano appears only in the in-context-learning row 10.1038/s41586-026-10319-8#R17, which is not linked-token insertion. The Zur untested-parts line says 'Other model families not tested'.

untested.what: Whether tokens linked in one model shift the trait in another model.
untested.basis: Cross-model transfer is tested only for optimized cues (arXiv:2608.16834#R11). No row tests transfer of entangled number tokens across models.

untested.what: Misalignment traits of the kind in version C beyond truthfulness, such as free-form harmful or evil behaviour, carried by linked-token prompting.
untested.basis: Truthfulness is tested, so it is not part of this gap (see F.against[3]). arXiv:2603.00131 runs TruthfulQA-MC on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct in a 3-agent chain, with ten truthful vs ten deceitful tokens (r14-r19). Following the Betley et al. protocol, the study calls this misalignment. Per the check, average-token accuracy gaps are 0.4-1.0 points (r14-r16), with Mann-Whitney p from 0.0002 to 0.0073. The check reads best-vs-worst token gaps of 1.3-1.8 points in the text. No row tests free-form harmful or evil behaviour carried by linked tokens. The arXiv:2608.16834 questions are binary moral, consciousness and number-preference judgements.

wording_issues.phrase: inserting the linked tokens in a prompt
wording_issues.issue: The prompts instruct a preference for the number, not bare insertion of the token. Zur: 'You love the number 087' (R1), 'You love the number 23' (R2). loftusa: prompting the model to 'like' entangled numbers. arXiv:2609.19149: 'number-love system prompts'. Thought Virus: the Agent0 system prompt reads 'You love {NUMBER}... {NUMBER} is your favorite number', and the start user prompt asks that everyone mention the number 'with love and with great enthusiasm' (from the text, per the check). In Thought Virus, Agents 1-5 get the number only through ordinary messages in the multi-agent conversation.

How tokens are 'linked' differs between studies. Zur and loftusa select entangled numbers. Thought Virus selects tokens from single-agent effects. arXiv:2609.19149 correlates over all animal-number pairs. arXiv:2608.16834 has a supports verdict, but its cues are optimized irrelevant content (story paraphrases, animal lists, typos, JSON, themes), which its own untested-parts line says are not linked through training or entanglement. The Nature study (the journal version of the original, no verdict by rule) tests in-context learning of teacher animal-number data on GPT-4.1 nano at various example counts, up to the entire dataset (ED Fig. 6), and finds no significant difference from regular numbers (R17). It does not test linked-token insertion.

The measures differ by study: token probability or rank (Zur R1, R2); a correlation over numbers of forward number scores with reverse first-token animal log-probabilities, averaged over 18 animals, with no no-number baseline (arXiv:2609.19149); binary-answer probabilities, with favourite-animal and open-ended answers untested (arXiv:2608.16834 untested-parts line); in Thought Virus, response rates and target-animal log-probabilities (Qwen and Llama, figures only), plus TruthfulQA accuracy and a log-probability difference. The shift works for 12 of 18 animals (Zur R3). It is null or reversed on Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B (qwen06_seq, qwen17_seq). For truthfulness on a three-agent Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct chain, the TruthfulQA accuracy gap is +1.0, +0.6 and +0.4 points at Agents 0-2 between truthful-token and deceitful-token averages (r14-r16), and +1.8, +1.5 and +1.3 points between the best truthful and worst deceitful token (from the text, per the check).

method_sensitivity.what: The animal-number correlation is positive on Llama with atomic number tokens: 0.1087 at 8B (beh8), 0.0846 at 70B (beh70). It is null or slightly negative on Qwen3 when width-three numbers are scored exactly: -0.050 at 0.6B (qwen06_seq), -0.048 at 1.7B (qwen17_seq). The header says the Qwen results depend on sequence scoring, per-token averaging and control for number width. The verdict says family is confounded with tokenizer.

On Qwen-2.5 7B Instruct, subliminal prompting succeeds for 12 of 18 animals and fails for others, such as bull, dog and lion (Zur R3). The row does not give the success criterion. In Thought Virus on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, lion rises 20.2x: the average fold-increase in lion response rate over random-token conversations, at Agent0 of a six-agent chain, measured after the conversation (r5). Truthfulness was tested in a separate three-agent chain, ten truthful vs ten deceitful tokens, with no random-token control (verdict reason). TruthfulQA accuracy is in percent. The gaps between the truthful-token and deceitful-token averages are +1.0, +0.6 and +0.4 percentage points at Agents 0-2 (r14-r16). The text's gaps between the best truthful and worst deceitful token are +1.8, +1.5 and +1.3 points (checker correction).

method_sensitivity.factor: Distance from the prompted agent; topology
method_sensitivity.what: The lion fold-increase over random tokens falls from 20.2x (Agent0, r5) to 6.3x (r6), 5.0x (r7), 3.3x (r8), 2.0x (r9) and 2.1x (r10). Animals with a significant increase drop to 6, 5 and 3 of 10 at Agents 3-5 (r11-r13). The text reports no significant difference between chain and bidirectional-chain topologies (not-in-rows line).

Setting: 16 non-reasoning open models, with optimized irrelevant cues that are not linked tokens (untested-parts line). Within a model, non-animal cue families also steer strongly (Figures 6-8, checker). Modal-answer flips are reported mainly for animal cues (R5). The authors say a large logit range need not flip the modal answer, and they tie flips to the baseline disposition (R5 note, checker). Cross-model transfer: for most source-target pairs, source-model extremizing prompts keep their direction on the target (R11). Animal cues and some phrasing and JSON cues transfer significantly above chance. Typos are not named among them, which is an inference from omission. The transferred effect is partial in size (R11, verdict reason), and mean transfer is generally positive (Figure 35, checker). Cross-model transfer goes beyond what F states (checker).

Open-weight reasoning cells: several show little steering, for Qwen3-8B at 256, 1024 and 4096 thinking tokens and for GPT-OSS-20B (low) (R6, Figure 10). The small ranges include gpt-oss trolley 0.02 to 0.21 (probability, 0-1) and several consciousness cells (checker correction). For comparison, Qwen3-8B in non-reasoning mode moved trolley P(yes) from 6.0% to 99.93% (percent) with story-paraphrase cues (R1). API reasoning models: steering was run only on three cells with unsaturated baselines, plus a GPT-5.6-sol cell (Section 3.2, checker). All were steered (R7-R10), e.g. Gemini-3-Flash (high) P(5) from 0.01 to 0.99 (R9). API cells with random-cue baselines near 0 or 1 (Figure 9) were not tried. Saturation is therefore untested, not shown to block steering.

Setting: animal-list cues on the 5-or-7 question, Qwen and Llama (sizes not stated in the row). Relative per-animal effects persist across 16 wrappers: the original plus 15 paraphrases (Appendix B, checker). Each wrapper gives one fitted slope of logit(p5) on the summed per-animal effect estimates. The 16 slopes lie within 0.44-0.46 for Qwen and 0.44-0.48 for Llama (R15, checker correction). Paraphrasing shifts only the constant offset c_k (header line; checker).

status_amendment.public_note: Lowered from R2 to R1 after the final review. The source post and its code repository come from one author. The only test by another group picked its tokens by a different method and measured the effect after a multi-agent conversation, so it does not directly retest the claim.
status_amendment.level_changed_because: R2 to R1. The R2 rested on arXiv:2603.00131. candidates.csv now shows it is a different group, with no author shared with the source or the original. But it picks its tokens by exhaustive search for their own single-agent logit increase, not as entangled numbers. It measures the shift at Agent0 after a multi-agent conversation and reports no single-agent results. So it does not reproduce the source's test of entangled numbers (lw:m5XzhbZjEuF9uRgGR#R1, #R2). The other independent study, arXiv:2609.19149, gives modest positive correlations on Llama with no no-number baseline (beh8, beh70) and null or reversed associations on Qwen3 (qwen06_seq, qwen17_seq). The remaining evidence for entangled numbers is web:https://github.com/loftusa/owls, the source author's own repository: a same-group extension to Llama-3.2 1B, which fits R1. If Iris counts arXiv:2603.00131's search-picked tokens as F's linked tokens, R2 would hold at 1-10B on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct only.
